confidence_explanation: The evidence shows a clear pattern of session hijacking followed by unauthorized cross-departmental data exfiltration. The mid-session IP change is a definitive indicator of hijacking, and the subsequent downloads of sensitive files from multiple departments (Finance, Engineering, Marketing, Executive) confirm a successful breach.

attack_chain.description: User_03 logs in successfully from their normal IP (192.168.1.103).
User_03 performs legitimate file reads within their own department (/data/hr/).
Session hijacking occurs: the same session_id (sess_user_03_20260728_001) is used from a new, external IP (91.219.236.222), and the user begins accessing unauthorized directories (/data/executive/).

The attacker begins exfiltrating data by downloading files from multiple unauthorized departments including Finance (evt_s61_009, evt_s61_010), Engineering (evt_s61_011), Marketing (evt_s61_012), and Shared Projects (evt_s61_013).
The attacker logs out, concluding the session.

gaps: Identification of the attacker's true location/identity via the IP 91.219.236.222.
Information on whether user_03's credentials were stolen via phishing or another method.
narrative: A session hijacking incident occurred where user_03's active session was hijacked by an external IP (91.219.236.222). The attacker leveraged this session to bypass departmental boundaries and exfiltrate sensitive files from the Executive, Finance, Engineering, Marketing, and Shared Project directories.
